title: Replace unchecked e.message as String? casts in PIN dialogs with a null-safe read
why: ArgumentError.message is typed Object? in dart:core, not String?. Both sites hard-cast it with `as String?`, which would throw a TypeError if PinService ever threw an ArgumentError constructed with a non-String message (e.g. ArgumentError.value(...)). Today PinService only ever throws `ArgumentError('PIN must be exactly 4 numeric digits')` so this never fires, but the cast is a landmine for the next caller of setProfilePin/setTutorPin-style methods that doesn't preserve that convention.
recommendation: Use `e.message?.toString() ?? <fallback>` instead of the unchecked cast in both places.
acceptance_criteria: Both sites read e.message without an unchecked String cast
A test constructing ArgumentError.value(42, 'pin') and feeding it through does not crash

corrections: dart:core declares ArgumentError.message as 'dynamic', not 'Object?' (cosmetic, same behavior). Separately, the proposed acceptance test ArgumentError.value(42, 'pin') sets message=null (3-arg form needed: e.g. ArgumentError.value(42,'pin',99)) so as literally written it would not reproduce the crash — the underlying defect claim is still valid, only the suggested regression test is imprecise.
